messages:
incident-bot:
:rotating_light: *Staged DR Drill Incident* opened by @Rafael Mendes
*Summary:* Restore-to-new-cluster drill failing during artifact fetch.
*Environment:* private-drill-01 (EKS, VPC-only)
*Runbook:* https://confluence.redwood.local/display/ENGPRIV/runbook-private-restore-to-new-cluster
*Dashboards:* https://grafana.redwood.local/d/private-backup-restore/private-backup-restore
*Owner:* SRE (on-point @Rafael Mendes)

Rafael Mendes:
Kicking off DR game day scenario: “lost control plane DB; restore to new cluster”. Restore Job is failing before it even gets to postgres restore. Looks like permissions on backup bucket / KMS.

Rafael Mendes:
Command we ran (from the new cluster jumpbox):
```bash
rw-private-dr restore plan \
  --cluster private-drill-01-new \
  --backup-uri s3://rw-private-backups-drill/cluster-private-drill-01/2025-11-26T1800Z \
  --out plan.json

rw-private-dr restore execute --plan plan.json --yes
```
It gets to “download artifacts” and dies.

incident-bot:
*Incident timeline started* (for evidence capture)
- Declared: 1732639922
- Severity: SEV-2 (drill)
- Incident channel: #incidents

Ethan Park:
Can you paste the restore job logs? Also which IAM role is the restore job using (IRSA)?

Bruno Silva:
+1, likely missing `kms:Decrypt` for SSE-KMS objects. We’ve hit this on a customer pilot when restore role != backup role.

Rafael Mendes:
Logs from the k8s Job `rw-private-restore-7c6b`:
```bash
kubectl -n redwood-private logs job/rw-private-restore-7c6b -c restore
```
Output:
```text
2025-11-26T18:41:09Z INFO  restore: starting restore execution (maintenance_mode=true)
2025-11-26T18:41:09Z INFO  restore: fetching backup manifest s3://rw-private-backups-drill/cluster-private-drill-01/2025-11-26T1800Z/manifest.json
2025-11-26T18:41:10Z INFO  restore: downloading artifact bundle artifacts.tar.zst
2025-11-26T18:41:12Z ERROR restore: failed to download artifacts
error="operation error S3: GetObject, https response error StatusCode: 403, RequestID: 7G9Y3Y..., HostID: 3k0...,
api error AccessDenied: Access Denied"
```
Then it retries 3x and bails.

Connor O'Brien:
Which service account is that pod using? If it’s `rw-private-dr` it should be `rw-private-dr-sa` in `redwood-private` ns.

Rafael Mendes:
Yup:
```bash
kubectl -n redwood-private get pod -l job-name=rw-private-restore-7c6b -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.serviceAccountName}'
# rw-private-dr-sa

kubectl -n redwood-private get sa rw-private-dr-sa -o yaml | sed -n '1,80p'
```
Annotation:
```yaml
eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::4411xxxxxx:role/rw-private-dr-restore
```

Marcus Lin:
If bucket is SSE-KMS (customer-owned key), `AccessDenied` could be either S3 policy or KMS key policy. AWS sometimes returns S3 403 when it’s actually KMS deny on decrypt.
Can you run `aws s3api head-object` from the same role and see if the error includes KMS?

Rafael Mendes:
From the jumpbox we assumed the same role:
```bash
aws sts get-caller-identity
# ... rw-private-dr-restore

aws s3api head-object \
  --bucket rw-private-backups-drill \
  --key cluster-private-drill-01/2025-11-26T1800Z/artifacts.tar.zst
```
Result:
```json
{
  "Error": {
    "Code": "403",
    "Message": "Forbidden"
  }
}
```
Not super helpful.

Allison Grant:
On the grafana panel “Backup/Restore job errors” I see `aws_error_code=AccessDenied` tagged with `stage=download_artifacts`. No more detail. We may want to emit the wrapped AWS SDK error fields (service + operation + request id) as labels or in structured logs.

Sean Gallagher:
Can we confirm the bucket policy allows the restore role? In the terraform examples I remember we scoped to the *backup writer* role and forgot read for restore (facepalm).

Bruno Silva:
Try `aws s3api get-object --range bytes=0-1` to see if it’s consistently denied.
Also check KMS key grants:
```bash
aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/rw-private-backups
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/rw-private-backups --policy-name default
```

Rafael Mendes:
Ok, bucket policy right now (redacted) basically:
- allow `s3:PutObject` / `s3:AbortMultipartUpload` to `rw-private-dr-backup`
- allow `s3:GetObject` to `rw-private-dr-backup`
No mention of `rw-private-dr-restore` role. So yeah, restore role can’t read.

Connor O'Brien:
That’s the bug then. For the drill: quickest workaround is either (a) use same role for backup+restore or (b) add read for restore role.
If we want to keep separate roles (preferred), patch bucket policy + KMS policy.

Marcus Lin:
If objects are SSE-KMS, also need:
- `kms:Decrypt` for restore role
- key policy must trust the role (or use grant)
And for backup role:
- `kms:Encrypt`, `kms:GenerateDataKey`

Markus Klein:
Just to keep the drill moving: ok to apply a break-glass read+decrypt policy? We should capture evidence + note it as follow-up to fix terraform module defaults.

Rafael Mendes:
:thumbsup: Doing minimal “read + decrypt” for restore role, scoped to bucket path prefix.
Applying bucket policy update now.

Rafael Mendes:
Bucket policy diff (sanitized):
```json
{
  "Sid": "AllowRestoreRoleRead",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::4411xxxxxx:role/rw-private-dr-restore"},
  "Action": ["s3:GetObject","s3:ListBucket"],
  "Resource": [
    "arn:aws:s3:::rw-private-backups-drill",
    "arn:aws:s3:::rw-private-backups-drill/cluster-private-drill-01/*"
  ]
}
```
Re-running restore job.

incident-bot:
:mag: *Reminder:* Capture artifacts for the retro
- exact error logs
- commands run
- policy changes (diff)
- time to mitigation

Rafael Mendes:
Restore job progressed further but now failing with a different 403:
```text
api error AccessDenied: Access to KMS is not allowed
```
So yep, KMS decrypt missing.

Marcus Lin:
Yup. Add IAM permission on the role *and* confirm KMS key policy allows it.
For IAM policy on `rw-private-dr-restore`:
```json
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:DescribeKey"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:4411xxxxxx:key/1f2a..."
}
```
If key policy is locked down, you’ll also need to add the role as a principal there.

Bruno Silva:
If the key is customer-managed, prefer updating key policy over wide grants. But for the drill we can do a scoped statement.

Rafael Mendes:
We own the key in this drill env. Updating key policy to allow decrypt for restore role. (Capturing in notes.)

Sahana Iyer:
Noting for follow-up: our integration test harness only covered S3 permissions, not KMS. We should add a negative test that restore role can actually read+decrypt.

Rafael Mendes:
Re-run `rw-private-dr restore execute` succeeded past artifact download. It’s now on DB restore step.

Ethan Park:
Nice. Please confirm maintenance mode is still on and control plane write paths are blocked (we had one case where it got toggled off early).

Rafael Mendes:
Checked:
```bash
rw-private-dr status --cluster private-drill-01-new | grep -i maintenance
# maintenance_mode: enabled

curl -k https://private-drill-01-new-api.redwood.private/v1/policies -X POST -d '{}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'
# 503 with message "Cluster is in maintenance mode (restore in progress). Try again after restore completes."
```
So that part looks good.

Allison Grant:
Can you add a note to include the KMS-specific error in the alert annotations? Right now it just pages “AccessDenied” with no hint it’s KMS vs S3.

Connor O'Brien:
Action item for installer/docs:
- In prerequisites for “restore to new cluster”, explicitly call out *restore role needs read + decrypt*.
- Add a `rw-private-dr restore preflight` check to test `GetObject` + a small decrypt read.

Sean Gallagher:
Agree. Also: terraform module should create both roles and wire policies (least privilege) by default. Separate roles is fine, but we need the correct minimum set.

Rafael Mendes:
Restore completed. Smoke tests passed. Total time lost to permissions: ~28 min.
Quick retro notes:
- Root cause: bucket policy + KMS key policy didn’t include `rw-private-dr-restore` role.
- Workaround: added `s3:GetObject/ListBucket` and `kms:Decrypt/DescribeKey` for restore role.
- Proposed fixes: terraform examples + preflight checks + improve error surfacing.
I’ll file follow-ups in Linear and attach policy diffs + logs.

incident-bot:
:white_check_mark: *Staged DR Drill Incident resolved*
- Resolved by: @Rafael Mendes
- Duration: 4816s
- Resolution note: Updated S3 bucket policy + KMS key policy to allow restore role to read and decrypt backup artifacts; re-ran restore successfully.
- Next: Link follow-ups in retro doc + game day tracker.
